title: When God Says, "You Do It."
chapterRef: Chapter 4: When God Says, "You Do It."

hero.alt: A small basket with five loaves and two fish, offered by open hands to a crowd.

hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
Maybe you're not lazy. Maybe you're tired from asking. God isn't mocking your weariness. Sometimes the kindest thing He does is narrow your world to one doable act.

Start smaller than your fear. If that's too much this week, your task is honesty and one trusted believer. Read "A Word to the Tired Prayer Warrior" when you can.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 4
read.body:
Open to Chapter 4, "When God Says, 'You Do It.'" Read "'Why Are You Crying to Me?'" and "Pray, and Post a Guard." Then read my story in "I've Lived the 'I'm Not Equipped' Freeze."

In the first section, Israel is trapped at the Red Sea, and God's answer to the cry is a staff already in Moses' hand. In the second, Nehemiah prays and sets a guard. Both. Not one or the other.

In my story, I tell you how I loved technology but told myself I couldn't execute without formal training, so ideas stayed ideas. When I demanded the whole task before I moved, I stayed stuck. Read it, then come back.

pulse.heading: The pulse: the staff is in your hand
pulse.body:
Sometimes the answer to the cry is a staff already in your hand.

Chapter 4 shows a pattern under the stories. God saves. God commands. And often He shows His power after the first obedient step. Israel marched before Jericho's walls fell. Moses lifted the staff before the sea opened.

You keep praying. You also move.

verses.text: The LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry to me? Tell the people of Israel to go forward. Lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, that the people of Israel may go through the sea on dry ground.

prompts: What did God tell Moses to do with what was already in his hand?

nameIt.heading: Name it: the lunch in the bag
nameIt.body:
The disciples saw a shortage. Jesus said, "You give them something to eat," and then asked what they had. Jesus multiplied it, and the disciples carried the baskets.

Chapter 4 also warns that waiting for perfect clarity can be delayed obedience. In a world of endless options, it's easy to keep researching. Don't outsource your obedience to one more opinion.

bookRef.chapter: Chapter 4: When God Says, "You Do It."
bookRef.section: "You Give Them Something to Eat"; Waiting for Perfect Clarity in a World of Options

verses.text: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” And they said to him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?” And he said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they had found out, they said, “Five, and two fish.”

prompts: What clear "You do it" step has been sitting on the table: a conversation, application, apology, build, or act of service?
Am I waiting for perfect conditions, or for courage to move with what I already have?
What's the "lunch in my bag" I keep overlooking?

build.heading: Build it: test it, then take it
build.body:
Not every risk is holy, so test the step. Chapter 4 gives five questions:

Is this already clear in Scripture? Have I been using prayer to postpone a known duty? What means has God already given me? Am I willing for the outcome to be His? Would mature believers call this faithfulness, or fear, pride, or impatience?

Then pray and post a guard, like Nehemiah. Dependence and diligence together.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 4:

Write the "You do it" step in one sentence. Pray a short prayer. Then take the step within 72 hours.

The chapter puts it plainly: often courage comes after obedience, not before. You don't have to feel brave to start. If 72 hours slips by, set a new time within three days and go.

help.heading: Help: bring one answer, walk with one person
help.body:
Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week. Tell them your "You do it" step and when you'll take it.

Then think of someone nearby who's carrying a lot. You don't need to tell them what to do. Ask, "Is there one thing I can carry with you this week?" Then carry it. The disciples carried baskets. So can we.

pray.heading: Pray it: short, then go
pray.body:
Long prayers that never leave the chair aren't always deeper. This one is short on purpose. Pray the line at the top of this screen, the one from Chapter 4, and then name your step.

My step is ____.

If you're carrying regret from a time you held back, bring it here too. In Chapter 4, "When I Waited for Perfect Clarity," I share my own regret and how I brought it to Christ. Some outcomes only God holds, and you don't have to carry them. Regret belongs at the cross, not in a life sentence.

Jesus, I bring You ____. Forgive what is mine to confess. Carry what was never mine to carry. Help me receive Your mercy and walk on. Amen.

review.heading: Review: what this is not
review.body:
After 72 hours, mark it honestly: took the step, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 4, "What This Is Not": not every risk is holy. This isn't earning. It doesn't deny that holy waiting is real. It isn't hustle. And it never asks you to be God. You take the step. God keeps the results.

If grief or regret came up this week, talk with a pastor or counselor. That's wisdom, not weakness.
